title: Banana Bread Pancakes with Brown Butter
changes_from_base: Mashed banana and brown sugar form the base, the butter is browned with cinnamon, and walnuts can be folded in; there is no soured cream.
summary: Pancakes infused with ripe banana and brown butter, warm with cinnamon, and studded with toasted walnuts for a comforting treat.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray
nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, plus more for the pan
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mash bananas
steps.text: Mash 2 large ripe bananas (about 400 g) with 1 tbsp dark brown sugar, 1 large egg and 1 tsp vanilla in a large bowl until mostly smooth.

steps.title: Brown butter
steps.text: Melt 42 g unsalted butter in a small pan over medium heat, stirring often, until the solids are golden brown and smell nutty (4-6 min); off the heat whisk in ¼ tsp ground cinnamon and cool 5 min.

steps.title: Mix dry
steps.text: Whisk 163 g plain flour, ¾ tsp baking powder, ¾ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ¼ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk the brown butter into the banana, then 120 ml buttermilk, then the flour mix until just combined; fold in 60 g toasted roughly chopped walnuts if using.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Set a wire rack in a rimmed baking tray. Heat a griddle to medium (175 °C) or a pan over medium heat; melt ½ tbsp butter, scoop 80 ml portions to make 8 cm pancakes (1-2.5 cm apart). Cook until bubbles appear and the base is golden (2-4 min), adjusting heat so they do not over-brown; flip and cook until cooked through (2-4 min). Move to the rack and repeat.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with 90 ml maple syrup.

tips: Brown butter—melted until the milk solids turn golden and nutty—adds depth that transforms these from simple banana pancakes into something richly flavoured.
Mashing the banana into the batter (rather than using it as a topping) means every bite has flavour throughout.
The walnuts are optional; fold them in last so they stay crunchy.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Once cool, they keep 5 days airtight in the fridge; reheat in the microwave or a 150 °C oven. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
